name: ProductCard
description: A product card shows one product in a grid or list: photo, name, short description, rating and price, with an optional sale price and actions. It is built from Card.
whenToUse: In product grids and lists: catalogs, search results, recommendations.

whenNotToUse.alternative: A page layout with the product details

anatomy.name: Photo
anatomy.description: Product image; the theme’s placeholder shows without one.

anatomy.name: Name
anatomy.description: The product name; the link in a clickable card.

anatomy.name: Rating
anatomy.description: Stars plus review count, announced in words.

anatomy.name: Price
anatomy.description: Current price in the brand color.

behavior.text: rating (0–5) is rounded to whole stars visually and announced exactly: “Rated 4.5 out of 5, 2,342 reviews”.
Prices are strings, formatted by your app for its currency and locale.
Wrap a card in ThemeProvider to show it in another brand.

content: Use the product’s real name; keep descriptions to one line in grids.

guidelines.do: Show the old price only for real discounts.
guidelines.why: Fake discounts erode trust and may break consumer law.

guidelines.do: Show ratings with their review count.
guidelines.dont: Show stars without saying how many reviews they’re based on.
guidelines.why: Five stars from two reviews means little.

guidelines.do: Link the whole card to the product page with href.
guidelines.dont: Add separate “View” links next to the title.
guidelines.why: One link per card keeps keyboard and screen reader navigation short.

keyboard.action: Reaches the card link and actions.

aria.when: Announces the rating and review count.

wcag.how: The rating has a text alternative; the photo is decorative next to the name.
The old price is struck through, not only colored.
All text passes 4.5:1 in every theme.

examples.title: Product
examples.description: A product on sale with a rating.
examples.code:
import { ProductCard } from '@ds/react';

<ProductCard
  title="Wireless headphones"
  description="Noise cancelling, 30-hour battery"
  imageUrl="/products/headphones.png"
  price="$299"
  oldPrice="$399"
  rating={4.5}
  reviews="2,342 reviews"
  href="/products/headphones"
/>

examples.title: With an action
examples.description: An add-to-cart button in the footer.
examples.code:
import { ProductCard, Button } from '@ds/react';

<ProductCard title="Smart watch" price="$199" actions={<Button size="small">Add to cart</Button>} />

examples.title: In another brand
examples.description: Scope a theme to one card.
examples.code:
import { ProductCard, ThemeProvider } from '@ds/react';

<ThemeProvider theme={{ brand: 'amber' }}>
  <ProductCard title="Leather bag" price="$149" />
</ThemeProvider>

related.relation: The container ProductCard is built from.

changes: Split from the old Card: rating in words, old price announced as “was”, themed via ThemeProvider instead of hard-coded brand colors.

components.name: ProductCard
components.description: A product in a grid or list: photo, name, rating and price. Built from Card.

description.description: One or two lines about the product.

imageUrl.description: Product photo. Without it, the theme's placeholder shows.

price.description: Current price, formatted for display, e.g. "$299".

oldPrice.description: Previous price, shown crossed out and announced as “was”.

rating.description: Average rating from 0 to 5. Shown as stars and announced in words.

actions.description: Buttons such as “Add to cart”. They stay clickable in a card with href.

labels.type: { rating?: ((rating: number) => string); was?: string; } | undefined

appearance.description:
`elevated` (default) lifts the card with the shadow theme, `outlined` draws a border for
dense layouts, `filled` tints it for grouping inside a surface.

orientation.description: `vertical` stacks media above the body; `horizontal` puts media beside it.

href.description:
Makes the whole card a link to this URL. The CardTitle becomes the link, and its hit area
covers the card, so there's one clear, accessible target.

as.description: Element to render: `article` (default) for standalone content, `div` or `li` otherwise.
